questions.q: Who coined the phrase “reality distortion field” for Steve Jobs?
a: Bud Tribble, a member of the Macintosh team
Walter Isaacson, his biographer
Steve Wozniak, his Apple co-founder
A journalist at Time Magazine
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Tribble borrowed the Star Trek term and applied it to Jobs’s ability to bend reality.

questions.q: What did the reality distortion field allow Jobs to do?
a: Convince people that impossible goals could be achieved
Predict which products would sell best
Avoid making decisions under pressure
Keep his team from disagreeing with him
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes him bending reality to his will and pushing engineers to attempt what seemed impossible.

questions.q: What does the summary call the major reason for the name Apple?
a: Apple comes before Atari in the phonebook
Apples were the only fruit Jobs would eat
The logo was designed by a friend
The name was chosen by a focus group
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the decisive business reason was appearing ahead of his former employer Atari in the listings.

questions.q: What made Steve Jobs a billionaire, according to the summary?
a: Pixar’s initial public offering
The launch of the iPhone
His salary as Apple’s chief executive
The sale of NeXT to Apple
questions.why: Lesson 3 says Pixar’s IPO gave him a twentyfold return and stock worth $1.2 billion.

questions.q: How did Jobs first acquire his stake in Pixar?
a: He bought a majority share from George Lucas for $5 million
He founded the company with his own animation team
He received it as part of a deal with Disney
He purchased shares on the open market after Toy Story
questions.why: Lesson 3 says he bought 80 percent from Lucas in 1986 and invested another $5 million.
